  1384→// InitializeSession creates session state for a new session or updates an existing one.
  1385→// This implements the optional SessionInitializer interface.
  1386→// Called during UserPromptSubmit to allow git hooks to detect active sessions.
  1387→//
  1388→// If the session already exists and HEAD has moved (e.g., user committed), updates
  1389→// BaseCommit to the new HEAD so future checkpoints go to the correct shadow branch.
  1390→//
  1391→// If there's an existing shadow branch with commits from a different session ID,
  1392→// returns a SessionIDConflictError to prevent orphaning existing session work.
  1393→//
  1394→// agentType is the human-readable name of the agent (e.g., "Claude Code").
  1395→// transcriptPath is the path to the live transcript file (for mid-session commit detection).
  1396→// userPrompt is the user's prompt text (stored truncated as FirstPrompt for display).
  1397→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) InitializeSession(sessionID string, agentType agent.AgentType, transcriptPath string, userPrompt string) error {
  1398→	repo, err := OpenRepository()
  1399→	if err != nil {
  1400→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to open git repository: %w", err)
  1401→	}
  1402→
  1403→	// Check if session already exists
  1404→	state, err := s.loadSessionState(sessionID)
  1405→	if err != nil {
  1406→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to check session state: %w", err)
  1407→	}
  1408→
  1409→	if state != nil && state.BaseCommit != "" {
  1410→		// Session is fully initialized — apply phase transition for TurnStart.
  1411→		if transErr := TransitionAndLog(state, session.EventTurnStart, session.TransitionContext{}, session.NoOpActionHandler{}); transErr != nil {
  1412→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[entire] Warning: turn start transition failed: %v\n", transErr)
  1413→		}
  1414→
  1415→		// Generate a new TurnID for each turn (correlates carry-forward checkpoints)
  1416→		turnID, err := id.Generate()
  1417→		if err != nil {
  1418→			return fmt.Errorf("failed to generate turn ID: %w", err)
  1419→		}
  1420→		state.TurnID = turnID.String()
  1421→
  1422→		// Backfill AgentType if empty or set to the generic default "Agent"
  1423→		if !isSpecificAgentType(state.AgentType) && agentType != "" {
  1424→			state.AgentType = agentType
  1425→		}
  1426→
  1427→		// Backfill FirstPrompt if empty (for sessions created before the first_prompt field was added)
  1428→		if state.FirstPrompt == "" && userPrompt != "" {
  1429→			state.FirstPrompt = truncatePromptForStorage(userPrompt)
  1430→		}
  1431→
  1432→		// Update transcript path if provided (may change on session resume)
  1433→		if transcriptPath != "" && state.TranscriptPath != transcriptPath {
  1434→			state.TranscriptPath = transcriptPath
  1435→		}
  1436→
  1437→		// Clear checkpoint IDs on every new prompt.
  1438→		// LastCheckpointID is set during PostCommit, cleared at new prompt.
  1439→		// TurnCheckpointIDs tracks mid-turn checkpoints for stop-time finalization.
  1440→		state.LastCheckpointID = ""
  1441→		state.TurnCheckpointIDs = nil
  1442→
  1443→		// Calculate attribution at prompt start (BEFORE agent makes any changes)
  1444→		// This captures user edits since the last checkpoint (or base commit for first prompt).
  1445→		// IMPORTANT: Always calculate attribution, even for the first checkpoint, to capture
  1446→		// user edits made before the first prompt. The inner CalculatePromptAttribution handles
  1447→		// nil lastCheckpointTree by falling back to baseTree.
  1448→		promptAttr := s.calculatePromptAttributionAtStart(repo, state)
  1449→		state.PendingPromptAttribution = &promptAttr
  1450→
  1451→		// Check if HEAD has moved (user pulled/rebased or committed)
  1452→		// migrateShadowBranchIfNeeded handles renaming the shadow branch and updating state.BaseCommit
  1453→		if _, err := s.migrateShadowBranchIfNeeded(repo, state); err != nil {
  1454→			return fmt.Errorf("failed to check/migrate shadow branch: %w", err)
  1455→		}
  1456→
  1457→		if err := s.saveSessionState(state); err != nil {
  1458→			return fmt.Errorf("failed to update session state: %w", err)
  1459→		}
  1460→		return nil
  1461→	}
  1462→	// If state exists but BaseCommit is empty, it's a partial state from concurrent warning
  1463→	// Continue below to properly initialize it
  1464→
  1465→	// Initialize new session
  1466→	state, err = s.initializeSession(repo, sessionID, agentType, transcriptPath, userPrompt)
  1467→	if err != nil {
  1468→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to initialize session: %w", err)
  1469→	}
  1470→
  1471→	// Apply phase transition: new session starts as ACTIVE.
  1472→	if transErr := TransitionAndLog(state, session.EventTurnStart, session.TransitionContext{}, session.NoOpActionHandler{}); transErr != nil {
  1473→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[entire] Warning: turn start transition failed: %v\n", transErr)
  1474→	}
  1475→
  1476→	// Calculate attribution for pre-prompt edits
  1477→	// This captures any user edits made before the first prompt
  1478→	promptAttr := s.calculatePromptAttributionAtStart(repo, state)
  1479→	state.PendingPromptAttribution = &promptAttr
  1480→	if err = s.saveSessionState(state); err != nil {
  1481→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to save attribution: %w", err)
  1482→	}
  1483→
  1484→	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Initialized shadow session: %s\n", sessionID)
  1485→	return nil
  1486→}
  1487→
  1488→// calculatePromptAttributionAtStart calculates attribution at prompt start (before agent runs).
  1489→// This captures user changes since the last checkpoint - no filtering needed since
  1490→// the agent hasn't made any changes yet.
  1491→//
  1492→// IMPORTANT: This reads from the worktree (not staging area) to match what WriteTemporary
  1493→// captures in checkpoints. If we read staged content but checkpoints capture worktree content,
  1494→// unstaged changes would be in the checkpoint but not counted in PromptAttribution, causing
  1495→// them to be incorrectly attributed to the agent later.
  1496→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) calculatePromptAttributionAtStart(
  1497→	repo *git.Repository,
  1498→	state *SessionState,
  1499→) PromptAttribution {
  1500→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "attribution")
  1501→	nextCheckpointNum := state.StepCount + 1
  1502→	result := PromptAttribution{CheckpointNumber: nextCheckpointNum}
  1503→
  1504→	// Get last checkpoint tree from shadow branch (if it exists)
  1505→	// For the first checkpoint, no shadow branch exists yet - this is fine,
  1506→	// CalculatePromptAttribution will use baseTree as the reference instead.
  1507→	var lastCheckpointTree *object.Tree
  1508→	shadowBranchName := checkpoint.ShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit, state.WorktreeID)
  1509→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName)
  1510→	ref, err := repo.Reference(refName, true)
  1511→	if err != nil {
  1512→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution: no shadow branch yet (first checkpoint)",
  1513→			slog.String("shadow_branch", shadowBranchName))
  1514→		// Continue with lastCheckpointTree = nil
  1515→	} else {
  1516→		shadowCommit, err := repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
  1517→		if err != nil {
  1518→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution: failed to get shadow commit",
  1519→				slog.String("shadow_ref", ref.Hash().String()),
  1520→				slog.String("error", err.Error()))
  1521→			// Continue with lastCheckpointTree = nil
  1522→		} else {
  1523→			lastCheckpointTree, err = shadowCommit.Tree()
  1524→			if err != nil {
  1525→				logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution: failed to get shadow tree",
  1526→					slog.String("error", err.Error()))
  1527→				// Continue with lastCheckpointTree = nil
  1528→			}
  1529→		}
  1530→	}
  1531→
  1532→	// Get base tree for agent lines calculation
  1533→	var baseTree *object.Tree
  1534→	if baseCommit, err := repo.CommitObject(plumbing.NewHash(state.BaseCommit)); err == nil {
  1535→		if tree, treeErr := baseCommit.Tree(); treeErr == nil {
  1536→			baseTree = tree
  1537→		} else {

  1539→				slog.String("error", treeErr.Error()))
  1540→		}

  1543→			slog.String("base_commit", state.BaseCommit),
  1544→			slog.String("error", err.Error()))
  1545→	}
  1546→

  1548→	if err != nil {
  1549→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution skipped: failed to get worktree",
  1550→			slog.String("error", err.Error()))

  1552→	}
  1553→

  1555→	status, err := worktree.Status()
  1556→	if err != nil {

  1558→			slog.String("error", err.Error()))

  1565→	// IMPORTANT: We read from worktree (not staging area) to match what WriteTemporary
  1566→	// captures in checkpoints. This ensures attribution is consistent.
  1567→	changedFiles := make(map[string]string)
  1568→	for filePath, fileStatus := range status {

  1570→		if fileStatus.Worktree == git.Unmodified && fileStatus.Staging == git.Unmodified {

  1574→		if strings.HasPrefix(filePath, paths.EntireMetadataDir+"/") || strings.HasPrefix(filePath, ".entire/") {

  1583→			// Binary files are excluded from line-based attribution calculations.

  1587→			}
  1588→		}

  1590→

  1592→	}

  1595→	result = CalculatePromptAttribution(baseTree, lastCheckpointTree, changedFiles, nextCheckpointNum)

  1600→// getStagedFiles returns a list of files staged for commit.
  1601→func getStagedFiles(repo *git.Repository) []string {
  1602→	worktree, err := repo.Worktree()
  1603→	if err != nil {
  1604→		return nil
  1605→	}
  1606→

  1608→	if err != nil {
  1609→		return nil

  1621→
  1622→// getLastPrompt retrieves the most recent user prompt from a session's shadow branch.
  1623→// Returns empty string if no prompt can be retrieved.
  1624→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) getLastPrompt(repo *git.Repository, state *SessionState) string {
  1625→	shadowBranchName := getShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit, state.WorktreeID)
  1626→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName)
  1627→	ref, err := repo.Reference(refName, true)
  1628→	if err != nil {
  1629→		return ""
  1630→	}
  1631→
  1632→	// Extract session data to get prompts for commit message generation
  1633→	// Pass agent type to handle different transcript formats (JSONL for Claude, JSON for Gemini)
  1634→	// Pass 0 for checkpointTranscriptStart since we're extracting all prompts, not calculating token usage
  1635→	sessionData, err := s.extractSessionData(repo, ref.Hash(), state.SessionID, nil, state.AgentType, "", 0)
  1636→	if err != nil || len(sessionData.Prompts) == 0 {
  1637→		return ""
  1638→	}
  1639→
  1640→	// Return the last prompt (most recent work before commit)
  1641→	return sessionData.Prompts[len(sessionData.Prompts)-1]
  1642→}
  1643→
  1644→// HandleTurnEnd dispatches strategy-specific actions emitted when an agent turn ends.
  1645→// The primary job is to finalize all checkpoints from this turn with the full transcript.
  1646→//
  1647→// During a turn, PostCommit writes provisional transcript data (whatever was available
  1648→// at commit time). HandleTurnEnd replaces that with the complete session transcript
  1649→// (from prompt to stop event), ensuring every checkpoint has the full context.
  1650→//
  1651→//nolint:unparam // error return required by interface but hooks must return nil
  1652→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) HandleTurnEnd(state *SessionState) error {
  1653→	// Finalize all checkpoints from this turn with the full transcript.
  1654→	//
  1655→	// IMPORTANT: This is best-effort - errors are logged but don't fail the hook.
  1656→	// Failing here would prevent session cleanup and could leave state inconsistent.
  1657→	// The provisional transcript from PostCommit is already persisted, so the
  1658→	// checkpoint isn't lost - it just won't have the complete transcript.
  1659→	errCount := s.finalizeAllTurnCheckpoints(state)
  1660→	if errCount > 0 {
  1661→		logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "checkpoint")
  1662→		logging.Warn(logCtx, "HandleTurnEnd completed with errors (best-effort)",
  1663→			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
  1664→			slog.Int("error_count", errCount),
  1665→		)
  1666→	}
  1667→	return nil
  1668→}
  1669→
  1670→// finalizeAllTurnCheckpoints replaces the provisional transcript in each checkpoint
  1671→// created during this turn with the full session transcript.
  1672→//
  1673→// This is called at turn end (stop hook). During the turn, PostCommit wrote whatever
  1674→// transcript was available at commit time. Now we have the complete transcript and
  1675→// replace it so every checkpoint has the full prompt-to-stop context.
  1676→//
  1677→// Returns the number of errors encountered (best-effort: continues processing on error).
  1678→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) finalizeAllTurnCheckpoints(state *SessionState) int {
  1679→	if len(state.TurnCheckpointIDs) == 0 {
  1680→		return 0 // No mid-turn commits to finalize
  1681→	}
  1682→
  1683→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "checkpoint")
  1684→
  1685→	logging.Info(logCtx, "finalizing turn checkpoints with full transcript",
  1686→		slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
  1687→		slog.Int("checkpoint_count", len(state.TurnCheckpointIDs)),
  1688→	)
  1689→
  1690→	errCount := 0
  1691→
  1692→	// Read full transcript from live transcript file
  1693→	if state.TranscriptPath == "" {
  1694→		logging.Warn(logCtx, "finalize: no transcript path, skipping",
  1695→			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
  1696→		)
  1697→		state.TurnCheckpointIDs = nil
  1698→		return 1 // Count as error - all checkpoints will be skipped
  1699→	}
  1700→
  1701→	fullTranscript, err := os.ReadFile(state.TranscriptPath)
  1702→	if err != nil || len(fullTranscript) == 0 {
  1703→		msg := "finalize: empty transcript, skipping"
  1704→		if err != nil {
  1705→			msg = "finalize: failed to read transcript, skipping"
  1706→		}
  1707→		logging.Warn(logCtx, msg,
  1708→			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
  1709→			slog.String("transcript_path", state.TranscriptPath),
  1710→			slog.Any("error", err),
  1711→		)
  1712→		state.TurnCheckpointIDs = nil
  1713→		return 1 // Count as error - all checkpoints will be skipped
  1714→	}
  1715→
  1716→	// Extract prompts and context from the full transcript
  1717→	prompts := extractUserPrompts(state.AgentType, string(fullTranscript))
  1718→	contextBytes := generateContextFromPrompts(prompts)
  1719→
  1720→	// Redact secrets before writing — matches WriteCommitted behavior.
  1721→	// The live transcript on disk contains raw content; redaction must happen
  1722→	// before anything is persisted to the metadata branch.
  1723→	fullTranscript, err = redact.JSONLBytes(fullTranscript)
  1724→	if err != nil {
  1725→		logging.Warn(logCtx, "finalize: transcript redaction failed, skipping",
  1726→			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
  1727→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
  1728→		)
  1729→		state.TurnCheckpointIDs = nil
  1730→		return 1 // Count as error - all checkpoints will be skipped
  1731→	}
  1732→	for i, p := range prompts {
  1733→		prompts[i] = redact.String(p)
  1734→	}
  1735→	contextBytes = redact.Bytes(contextBytes)
  1736→
  1737→	// Open repository and create checkpoint store
  1738→	repo, err := OpenRepository()
  1739→	if err != nil {
  1740→		logging.Warn(logCtx, "finalize: failed to open repository",
  1741→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
  1742→		)
  1743→		state.TurnCheckpointIDs = nil
  1744→		return 1 // Count as error - all checkpoints will be skipped
  1745→	}
  1746→	store := checkpoint.NewGitStore(repo)
  1747→
  1748→	// Update each checkpoint with the full transcript
  1749→	for _, cpIDStr := range state.TurnCheckpointIDs {
  1750→		cpID, parseErr := id.NewCheckpointID(cpIDStr)
  1751→		if parseErr != nil {
  1752→			logging.Warn(logCtx, "finalize: invalid checkpoint ID, skipping",
  1753→				slog.String("checkpoint_id", cpIDStr),
  1754→				slog.String("error", parseErr.Error()),
  1755→			)
  1756→			errCount++
  1757→			continue
  1758→		}
  1759→
  1760→		updateErr := store.UpdateCommitted(context.Background(), checkpoint.UpdateCommittedOptions{
  1761→			CheckpointID: cpID,
  1762→			SessionID:    state.SessionID,
  1763→			Transcript:   fullTranscript,
  1764→			Prompts:      prompts,
  1765→			Context:      contextBytes,
  1766→			Agent:        state.AgentType,
  1767→		})
  1768→		if updateErr != nil {
  1769→			logging.Warn(logCtx, "finalize: failed to update checkpoint",
  1770→				slog.String("checkpoint_id", cpIDStr),
  1771→				slog.String("error", updateErr.Error()),
  1772→			)
  1773→			errCount++
  1774→			continue
  1775→		}
  1776→
  1777→		logging.Info(logCtx, "finalize: checkpoint updated with full transcript",
  1778→			slog.String("checkpoint_id", cpIDStr),
  1779→			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
  1780→		)
  1781→	}
  1782→
  1783→	// Clear turn checkpoint IDs. Do NOT update CheckpointTranscriptStart here — it was
  1784→	// already set correctly by PostCommit: condenseAndUpdateState sets it to the total
  1785→	// transcript lines when condensing, and carryForwardToNewShadowBranch resets it to 0
  1786→	// when carry-forward is active. Overwriting here would break carry-forward by making
  1787→	// sessionHasNewContent think the transcript is fully consumed (no growth).
  1788→	state.TurnCheckpointIDs = nil
  1789→
  1790→	return errCount
  1791→}
  1792→
  1793→// filesChangedInCommit returns the set of files changed in a commit by diffing against its parent.
  1794→func filesChangedInCommit(commit *object.Commit) map[string]struct{} {
  1795→	result := make(map[string]struct{})
  1796→
  1797→	commitTree, err := commit.Tree()
  1798→	if err != nil {
  1799→		return result
  1800→	}
  1801→
  1802→	var parentTree *object.Tree
  1803→	if commit.NumParents() > 0 {
  1804→		parent, err := commit.Parent(0)
  1805→		if err != nil {
  1806→			return result
  1807→		}
  1808→		parentTree, err = parent.Tree()
  1809→		if err != nil {
  1810→			return result
  1811→		}
  1812→	}
  1813→
  1814→	if parentTree == nil {
  1815→		// Initial commit — all files are new
  1816→		if iterErr := commitTree.Files().ForEach(func(f *object.File) error {
  1817→			result[f.Name] = struct{}{}
  1818→			return nil
  1819→		}); iterErr != nil {
  1820→			return result
  1821→		}
  1822→		return result
  1823→	}
  1824→
  1825→	changes, err := parentTree.Diff(commitTree)
  1826→	if err != nil {
  1827→		return result
  1828→	}
  1829→	for _, change := range changes {
  1830→		name := change.To.Name
  1831→		if name == "" {
  1832→			name = change.From.Name
  1833→		}
  1834→		result[name] = struct{}{}
  1835→	}
  1836→	return result
  1837→}
  1838→
  1839→// subtractFiles returns files that are NOT in the exclude set.
  1840→func subtractFiles(files []string, exclude map[string]struct{}) []string {
  1841→	var remaining []string
  1842→	for _, f := range files {
  1843→		if _, excluded := exclude[f]; !excluded {
  1844→			remaining = append(remaining, f)
  1845→		}
  1846→	}
  1847→	return remaining
  1848→}
  1849→
  1850→// carryForwardToNewShadowBranch creates a new shadow branch at the current HEAD
  1851→// containing the remaining uncommitted files and all session metadata.
  1852→// This enables the next commit to get its own unique checkpoint.
  1853→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) carryForwardToNewShadowBranch(
  1854→	logCtx context.Context,
  1855→	repo *git.Repository,
  1856→	state *SessionState,
  1857→	remainingFiles []string,
  1858→) {
  1859→	store := checkpoint.NewGitStore(repo)
  1860→
  1861→	// Don't include metadata directory in carry-forward. The carry-forward branch
  1862→	// only needs to preserve file content for comparison - not the transcript.
  1863→	// Including the transcript would cause sessionHasNewContent to always return true
  1864→	// because CheckpointTranscriptStart is reset to 0 for carry-forward.
  1865→	result, err := store.WriteTemporary(context.Background(), checkpoint.WriteTemporaryOptions{
  1866→		SessionID:         state.SessionID,
  1867→		BaseCommit:        state.BaseCommit,
  1868→		WorktreeID:        state.WorktreeID,
  1869→		ModifiedFiles:     remainingFiles,
  1870→		MetadataDir:       "",
  1871→		MetadataDirAbs:    "",
  1872→		CommitMessage:     "carry forward: uncommitted session files",
  1873→		IsFirstCheckpoint: false,
  1874→	})
  1875→	if err != nil {
  1876→		logging.Warn(logCtx, "post-commit: carry-forward failed",
  1877→			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
  1878→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
  1879→		)
  1880→		return
  1881→	}
  1882→	if result.Skipped {
  1883→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "post-commit: carry-forward skipped (no changes)",
  1884→			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
  1885→		)
  1886→		return
  1887→	}
  1888→
  1889→	// Update state for the carry-forward checkpoint.
  1890→	// CheckpointTranscriptStart = 0 is intentional: each checkpoint is self-contained with
  1891→	// the full transcript. This trades storage efficiency for simplicity:
  1892→	// - Pro: Each checkpoint is independently readable without needing to stitch together
  1893→	//   multiple checkpoints to understand the session history
  1894→	// - Con: For long sessions with multiple partial commits, each checkpoint includes
  1895→	//   the full transcript, which could be large
  1896→	// An alternative would be incremental checkpoints (only new content since last condensation),
  1897→	// but this would complicate checkpoint retrieval and require careful tracking of dependencies.
  1898→	state.StepCount = 1
  1899→	state.CheckpointTranscriptStart = 0
  1900→	state.LastCheckpointID = ""
  1901→	// NOTE: TurnCheckpointIDs is intentionally NOT cleared here. Those checkpoint
  1902→	// IDs from earlier in the turn still need finalization with the full transcript
  1903→	// when HandleTurnEnd runs at stop time.
  1904→
  1905→	logging.Info(logCtx, "post-commit: carried forward remaining files",
  1906→		slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
  1907→		slog.Int("remaining_files", len(remainingFiles)),
  1908→	)
  1909→}

   539→   539→// TestE2E_ContentAwareOverlap_RevertAndReplace tests content-aware overlap detection
   540→   540→// when user reverts session changes and writes different content.
   541→   541→//
   542→   542→// Content-Aware Overlap Detection:
   543→   543→// - Agent creates file X with content "hello"
   544→   544→// - User reverts X (git checkout -- X)
   545→   545→// - User writes completely different content
   546→   546→// - User commits
   547→   547→// - Content mismatch → NO checkpoint trailer added
   548→   548→func TestE2E_ContentAwareOverlap_RevertAndReplace(t *testing.T) {
   549→   549→	t.Parallel()
   550→   550→
   551→   551→	env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t, "manual-commit")
   552→   552→
   553→   553→	// Agent creates a file
   554→   554→	t.Log("Agent creating file with specific content")
   555→   555→	createPrompt := `Create a file called overlap_test.go with this exact content:
   556→   556→package main
   557→   557→
   558→   558→func OverlapOriginal() string {
   559→   559→	return "original content from agent"
   560→   560→}
   561→   561→
   562→   562→Create only this file.`
   563→   563→
   564→   564→	result, err := env.RunAgent(createPrompt)
   565→   565→	require.NoError(t, err)
   566→   566→	AssertAgentSuccess(t, result, err)
   567→   567→
   568→   568→	require.True(t, env.FileExists("overlap_test.go"))
   569→   569→	originalContent := env.ReadFile("overlap_test.go")
   570→   570→	t.Logf("Original content: %s", originalContent)
   571→   571→
   572→   572→	// Verify rewind points exist (session tracked the change)
   573→   573→	points := env.GetRewindPoints()
   574→   574→	require.GreaterOrEqual(t, len(points), 1, "Should have rewind points")
   575→   575→
   576→   576→	// User reverts the file and writes completely different content
   577→   577→	t.Log("User reverting file and writing different content")
   578→   578→	differentContent := `package main
   579→   579→
   580→   580→func CompletelyDifferent() string {
   581→   581→	return "user wrote this, not the agent"
   582→   582→}
   583→   583→`
   584→   584→	env.WriteFile("overlap_test.go", differentContent)
   585→   585→
   586→   586→	// Verify content is different
   587→   587→	currentContent := env.ReadFile("overlap_test.go")
   588→   588→	assert.NotEqual(t, originalContent, currentContent)
   589→   589→
   590→   590→	// Commits before this test
   591→   591→	commitsBefore := env.GetCommitCount()
   592→   592→
   593→   593→	// User commits the different content
   594→   594→	t.Log("Committing user-written content")
   595→   595→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add overlap test file", "overlap_test.go")
   596→   596→
   597→   597→	// Verify commit was made
   598→   598→	commitsAfter := env.GetCommitCount()
   599→   599→	assert.Equal(t, commitsBefore+1, commitsAfter, "Should have one new commit")
   600→   600→
   601→   601→	// Check for checkpoint trailer
   602→   602→	// With content-aware overlap detection, if the user completely replaced
   603→   603→	// the agent's content (new file with different hash), there should be
   604→   604→	// NO checkpoint trailer added. This is documented in checkpoint-scenarios.md
   605→   605→	// under "Content-Aware Overlap Detection".
   606→   606→	checkpointIDs := env.GetAllCheckpointIDsFromHistory()
   607→   607→	t.Logf("Checkpoint IDs found: %v", checkpointIDs)
   608→   608→
   609→   609→	// The first commit (Initial commit from NewFeatureBranchEnv) doesn't have a checkpoint.
   610→   610→	// Only agent-assisted commits should have checkpoint trailers.
   611→   611→	// When user completely replaces agent content, content-aware detection should
   612→   612→	// prevent the checkpoint trailer from being added.
   613→   613→	//
   614→   614→	// Per docs/architecture/checkpoint-scenarios.md:
   615→   615→	// - New file + content hash mismatch → No overlap → No checkpoint trailer
   616→   616→	assert.Empty(t, checkpointIDs,
   617→   617→		"Content-aware detection should prevent checkpoint trailer when user completely replaces agent content")
   618→   618→}

   620→   620→// TestE2E_Scenario1_BasicFlow verifies the simplest workflow matches the documented scenario.
   621→   621→//
   622→   622→// Scenario 1: Prompt → Changes → Prompt Finishes → User Commits
   623→   623→// This test explicitly verifies the documented flow.
   624→   624→func TestE2E_Scenario1_BasicFlow(t *testing.T) {
   625→   625→	t.Parallel()
   626→   626→
   627→   627→	env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t, "manual-commit")
   628→   628→
   629→   629→	// 1. User submits prompt (triggers UserPromptSubmit hook → InitializeSession)
   630→   630→	t.Log("Step 1: User submits prompt")
   631→   631→
   632→   632→	// 2. Claude makes changes (creates files)
   633→   633→	prompt := `Create a file called scenario1.go with this content:
   634→   634→package main

   637→   637→
   638→   638→	result, err := env.RunAgent(prompt)
   639→   639→	require.NoError(t, err)
   640→   640→	AssertAgentSuccess(t, result, err)
   641→   641→
   642→   642→	// Verify file was created
   643→   643→	require.True(t, env.FileExists("scenario1.go"))
   644→   644→
   645→   645→	// 3. After stop hook: checkpoint is saved, FilesTouched is set
   646→   646→	t.Log("Step 3: Checking rewind points after stop")
   647→   647→	points := env.GetRewindPoints()
   648→   648→	require.GreaterOrEqual(t, len(points), 1, "Should have rewind point after stop")
   649→   649→	t.Logf("Rewind points: %d", len(points))

   779→   779→// TestE2E_ExistingFiles_StashModifications tests stashing modifications to
   780→   780→// tracked files (not new untracked files). This exercises the standard git stash
   781→   781→// behavior (without -u flag) since modifications to tracked files are stashable.
   782→   782→func TestE2E_ExistingFiles_StashModifications(t *testing.T) {
   783→   783→	t.Parallel()
   784→   784→
   785→   785→	env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t, "manual-commit")
   786→   786→
   787→   787→	// Create and commit two existing files
   788→   788→	env.WriteFile("fileA.go", "package main\n\nfunc A() { /* original */ }\n")
   789→   789→	env.WriteFile("fileB.go", "package main\n\nfunc B() { /* original */ }\n")
   790→   790→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add initial files", "fileA.go", "fileB.go")
   791→   791→
   792→   792→	// Agent modifies both files
   793→   793→	t.Log("Agent modifying fileA.go and fileB.go")
   794→   794→	prompt := `Modify these files:
   795→   795→1. In fileA.go, change the comment from "original" to "modified by agent"
   796→   796→2. In fileB.go, change the comment from "original" to "modified by agent"
   797→   797→Only modify these two files.`
   798→   798→
   799→   799→	result, err := env.RunAgent(prompt)
   800→   800→	require.NoError(t, err)
   801→   801→	AssertAgentSuccess(t, result, err)
   802→   802→
   803→   803→	// Verify both files were modified
   804→   804→	contentA := env.ReadFile("fileA.go")
   805→   805→	contentB := env.ReadFile("fileB.go")
   806→   806→	assert.Contains(t, contentA, "modified by agent", "fileA.go should be modified")
   807→   807→	assert.Contains(t, contentB, "modified by agent", "fileB.go should be modified")
   808→   808→
   809→   809→	// User commits only fileA.go
   810→   810→	t.Log("Committing only fileA.go")
   811→   811→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Update fileA", "fileA.go")
   812→   812→	checkpoint1 := env.GetLatestCheckpointID()
   813→   813→	require.NotEmpty(t, checkpoint1, "First commit should have checkpoint")
   814→   814→
   815→   815→	// User stashes fileB.go modifications (tracked file, standard stash works)
   816→   816→	t.Log("Stashing fileB.go modifications")
   817→   817→	env.GitStash()
   818→   818→
   819→   819→	// Verify fileB.go is reverted to original
   820→   820→	contentB = env.ReadFile("fileB.go")
   821→   821→	assert.Contains(t, contentB, "original", "fileB.go should be reverted after stash")
   822→   822→	assert.NotContains(t, contentB, "modified by agent", "fileB.go should not have agent changes")
   823→   823→
   824→   824→	// User pops the stash and commits fileB.go
   825→   825→	t.Log("Popping stash and committing fileB.go")
   826→   826→	env.GitStashPop()
   827→   827→	contentB = env.ReadFile("fileB.go")
   828→   828→	assert.Contains(t, contentB, "modified by agent", "fileB.go should have agent changes after stash pop")
   829→   829→
   830→   830→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Update fileB", "fileB.go")
   831→   831→	checkpoint2 := env.GetLatestCheckpointID()
   832→   832→
   833→   833→	// Both commits should have checkpoints
   834→   834→	require.NotEmpty(t, checkpoint2, "Second commit should have checkpoint")
   835→   835→	assert.NotEqual(t, checkpoint1, checkpoint2, "Checkpoints should be different")
   836→   836→
   837→   837→	t.Logf("Checkpoint 1: %s, Checkpoint 2: %s", checkpoint1, checkpoint2)
   838→   838→}

   914→   914→// TestE2E_ExistingFiles_RevertModification tests that modifying an existing file
   915→   915→// that was touched by the session ALWAYS gets a checkpoint, even if the user writes
   916→   916→// completely different content.
   917→   917→//
   918→   918→// This is intentional behavior: for files that already exist in HEAD (modified files),
   919→   919→// we always count as overlap because the user is editing a file the session worked on.
   920→   920→// Content-aware detection only applies to NEW files (don't exist in HEAD).
   921→   921→//
   922→   922→// See content_overlap.go for the rationale.
   923→   923→func TestE2E_ExistingFiles_RevertModification(t *testing.T) {
   924→   924→	t.Parallel()
   925→   925→
   926→   926→	env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t, "manual-commit")
   927→   927→
   928→   928→	// Create and commit an existing file
   929→   929→	originalContent := `package main
   930→   930→
   931→   931→// placeholder
   932→   932→`
   933→   933→	env.WriteFile("calc.go", originalContent)
   934→   934→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add placeholder", "calc.go")
   935→   935→
   936→   936→	// Agent modifies the existing file
   937→   937→	t.Log("Agent modifying calc.go")
   938→   938→	prompt := `Replace the contents of calc.go with this exact code:
   939→   939→package main
   940→   940→
   941→   941→func AgentMultiply(a, b int) int {
   942→   942→	return a * b
   943→   943→}
   944→   944→
   945→   945→Only modify calc.go, nothing else.`
   946→   946→
   947→   947→	result, err := env.RunAgent(prompt)
   948→   948→	require.NoError(t, err)
   949→   949→	AssertAgentSuccess(t, result, err)
   950→   950→
   951→   951→	// Verify agent modified the file
   952→   952→	modifiedContent := env.ReadFile("calc.go")
   953→   953→	assert.Contains(t, modifiedContent, "AgentMultiply", "calc.go should have AgentMultiply function")
   954→   954→
   955→   955→	// User reverts and writes completely different content
   956→   956→	t.Log("User reverting and writing completely different content")
   957→   957→	userContent := `package main
   958→   958→
   959→   959→func UserAdd(x, y int) int {
   960→   960→	return x + y
   961→   961→}
   962→   962→`
   963→   963→	env.WriteFile("calc.go", userContent)
   964→   964→
   965→   965→	// User commits their changes
   966→   966→	t.Log("Committing user's changes")
   967→   967→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add user functions", "calc.go")
   968→   968→
   969→   969→	// For MODIFIED files (existing in HEAD), we always count as overlap.
   970→   970→	// The checkpoint SHOULD be created even though content is different.
   971→   971→	// This is because the session touched this file, so any commit to it
   972→   972→	// should be linked to preserve the editing history.
   973→   973→	checkpointIDs := env.GetAllCheckpointIDsFromHistory()
   974→   974→	t.Logf("Checkpoint IDs: %v", checkpointIDs)
   975→   975→
   976→   976→	latestCheckpoint := env.GetLatestCheckpointID()
   977→   977→	assert.NotEmpty(t, latestCheckpoint,
   978→   978→		"Modified files should always get checkpoint (content-aware only applies to new files)")
   979→   979→}

  1031→  1031→// TestE2E_EndedSession_UserCommitsAfterExit tests that after agent exits
  1032→  1032→// (session naturally ends), user commits still get checkpoint trailers.
  1033→  1033→// This exercises the ENDED + GitCommit → ActionCondenseIfFilesTouched path.
  1034→  1034→func TestE2E_EndedSession_UserCommitsAfterExit(t *testing.T) {

  1038→  1038→

  1040→  1040→	prompt := `Create these files:
  1041→  1041→1. ended_a.go with content: package main; func EndedA() {}
  1042→  1042→2. ended_b.go with content: package main; func EndedB() {}
  1043→  1043→3. ended_c.go with content: package main; func EndedC() {}
  1044→  1044→Create all three files, nothing else.`
  1045→  1045→
  1046→  1046→	result, err := env.RunAgent(prompt)
  1047→  1047→	require.NoError(t, err)
  1048→  1048→	AssertAgentSuccess(t, result, err)
  1049→  1049→
  1050→  1050→	require.True(t, env.FileExists("ended_a.go"), "ended_a.go should exist")
  1051→  1051→	require.True(t, env.FileExists("ended_b.go"), "ended_b.go should exist")
  1052→  1052→	require.True(t, env.FileExists("ended_c.go"), "ended_c.go should exist")
  1053→  1053→
  1054→  1054→	// User commits A and B together
  1055→  1055→	t.Log("Committing ended_a.go and ended_b.go")
  1056→  1056→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add ended files A and B", "ended_a.go", "ended_b.go")
  1057→  1057→	checkpointIDsAfterFirst := env.GetAllCheckpointIDsFromHistory()
  1058→  1058→	require.GreaterOrEqual(t, len(checkpointIDsAfterFirst), 1, "Should have first checkpoint")
  1059→  1059→	checkpointAB := checkpointIDsAfterFirst[0]
  1060→  1060→	t.Logf("Checkpoint for A,B: %s", checkpointAB)
  1061→  1061→
  1062→  1062→	// User commits C
  1063→  1063→	t.Log("Committing ended_c.go")

   427→   427→// GitCommitWithTrailerRemoved stages and commits files, simulating what happens when
   428→   428→// a user removes the Entire-Checkpoint trailer during commit message editing.
   429→   429→// This tests the opt-out behavior where removing the trailer skips condensation.
   430→   430→func (env *TestEnv) GitCommitWithTrailerRemoved(message string, files ...string) {
   431→   431→	env.T.Helper()
   432→   432→
   433→   433→	// Stage files using go-git
   434→   434→	for _, file := range files {
   435→   435→		env.GitAdd(file)
   436→   436→	}
   437→   437→
   438→   438→	// Create a temp file for the commit message
   439→   439→	msgFile := filepath.Join(env.RepoDir, ".git", "COMMIT_EDITMSG")
   440→   440→	//nolint:gosec // test code, permissions are intentionally standard
   441→   441→	if err := os.WriteFile(msgFile, []byte(message), 0o644); err != nil {
   442→   442→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to write commit message file: %v", err)
   443→   443→	}
   444→   444→
   445→   445→	// Run prepare-commit-msg hook
   446→   446→	//nolint:gosec,noctx // test code, args are from trusted test setup, no context needed
   447→   447→	prepCmd := exec.Command(getTestBinary(), "hooks", "git", "prepare-commit-msg", msgFile)
   448→   448→	prepCmd.Dir = env.RepoDir
   449→   449→	prepCmd.Env = append(os.Environ(),
   450→   450→		"ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=1",
   451→   451→		"ENTIRE_TEST_CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="+filepath.Join(env.RepoDir, ".claude"),
   452→   452→		"ENTIRE_TEST_GEMINI_PROJECT_DIR="+filepath.Join(env.RepoDir, ".gemini"),
   453→   453→	)
   454→   454→	if output, err := prepCmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
   455→   455→		env.T.Logf("prepare-commit-msg output: %s", output)
   456→   456→	}
   457→   457→
   458→   458→	// Read the modified message (with trailer added by hook)
   459→   459→	//nolint:gosec // test code, path is from test setup
   460→   460→	modifiedMsg, err := os.ReadFile(msgFile)
   461→   461→	if err != nil {
   462→   462→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to read modified commit message: %v", err)
   463→   463→	}
   464→   464→
   465→   465→	// REMOVE the Entire-Checkpoint trailer (simulating user editing the message)
   466→   466→	lines := strings.Split(string(modifiedMsg), "\n")
   467→   467→	var cleanedLines []string
   468→   468→	for _, line := range lines {
   469→   469→		if strings.HasPrefix(line, "Entire-Checkpoint:") {
   470→   470→			continue
   471→   471→		}
   472→   472→		if strings.Contains(line, "Remove the Entire-Checkpoint trailer") {
   473→   473→			continue
   474→   474→		}
   475→   475→		if strings.Contains(line, "trailer will be added to your next commit") {
   476→   476→			continue
   477→   477→		}
   478→   478→		cleanedLines = append(cleanedLines, line)
   479→   479→	}
   480→   480→	cleanedMsg := strings.TrimRight(strings.Join(cleanedLines, "\n"), "\n") + "\n"
   481→   481→
   482→   482→	// Create the commit using go-git with the cleaned message (no trailer)
   483→   483→	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(env.RepoDir)
   484→   484→	if err != nil {
   485→   485→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to open git repo: %v", err)

   499→   499→	})

   501→   501→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to commit: %v", err)

   694→   694→// GetLatestCheckpointIDFromHistory walks backwards from HEAD and returns
   695→   695→// the checkpoint ID from the first commit with an Entire-Checkpoint trailer.
   696→   696→// Returns an error if no checkpoint trailer is found in any commit.
   697→   697→func (env *TestEnv) GetLatestCheckpointIDFromHistory() (string, error) {
   698→   698→	env.T.Helper()
   699→   699→
   700→   700→	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(env.RepoDir)
   701→   701→	if err != nil {
   702→   702→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to open git repo: %v", err)
   703→   703→	}
   704→   704→
   705→   705→	head, err := repo.Head()
   706→   706→	if err != nil {
   707→   707→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to get HEAD: %v", err)
   708→   708→	}
   709→   709→
   710→   710→	commitIter, err := repo.Log(&git.LogOptions{From: head.Hash()})
   711→   711→	if err != nil {
   712→   712→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to iterate commits: %v", err)
   713→   713→	}
   714→   714→
   715→   715→	var checkpointID string
   716→   716→	//nolint:errcheck,gosec // ForEach callback returns error to stop iteration, not a real error
   717→   717→	commitIter.ForEach(func(c *object.Commit) error {
   718→   718→		// Look for Entire-Checkpoint trailer
   719→   719→		for _, line := range strings.Split(c.Message, "\n") {
   720→   720→			line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
   721→   721→			if strings.HasPrefix(line, "Entire-Checkpoint:") {
   722→   722→				checkpointID = strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(line, "Entire-Checkpoint:"))
   723→   723→				return errors.New("stop iteration")
   724→   724→			}
   725→   725→		}
   726→   726→		return nil
   727→   727→	})
   728→   728→
   729→   729→	if checkpointID == "" {
   730→   730→		return "", errors.New("no commit with Entire-Checkpoint trailer found in history")
   731→   731→	}
   732→   732→
   733→   733→	return checkpointID, nil
   734→   734→}

  1008→  1008→// ValidateCheckpoint performs comprehensive validation of a checkpoint on the metadata branch.
  1009→  1009→func (env *TestEnv) ValidateCheckpoint(v CheckpointValidation) {
  1010→  1010→	env.T.Helper()
  1011→  1011→
  1012→  1012→	metadataBranch := "entire/checkpoints/v1"
  1013→  1013→
  1014→  1014→	// Compute sharded path: <id[:2]>/<id[2:]>/
  1015→  1015→	if len(v.CheckpointID) < 3 {
  1016→  1016→		env.T.Fatalf("Checkpoint ID too short: %s", v.CheckpointID)
  1017→  1017→	}
  1018→  1018→	shardedPath := v.CheckpointID[:2] + "/" + v.CheckpointID[2:]
  1019→  1019→
  1020→  1020→	// Validate root metadata.json exists and has expected fields
  1021→  1021→	summaryPath := shardedPath + "/metadata.json"
  1022→  1022→	summaryContent, found := env.ReadFileFromBranch(metadataBranch, summaryPath)
  1023→  1023→	if !found {
  1024→  1024→		env.T.Errorf("CheckpointSummary not found at %s", summaryPath)
  1025→  1025→	} else {
  1026→  1026→		var summary map[string]any
  1027→  1027→		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(summaryContent), &summary); err != nil {
  1028→  1028→			env.T.Errorf("Failed to parse CheckpointSummary: %v", err)
  1029→  1029→		} else {
  1030→  1030→			// Validate checkpoint_id
  1031→  1031→			if cpID, ok := summary["checkpoint_id"].(string); !ok || cpID != v.CheckpointID {
  1032→  1032→				env.T.Errorf("CheckpointSummary.checkpoint_id = %v, want %s", summary["checkpoint_id"], v.CheckpointID)
  1033→  1033→			}
  1034→  1034→			// Validate strategy if specified
  1035→  1035→			if v.Strategy != "" {
  1036→  1036→				if strategy, ok := summary["strategy"].(string); !ok || strategy != v.Strategy {
  1037→  1037→					env.T.Errorf("CheckpointSummary.strategy = %v, want %s", summary["strategy"], v.Strategy)
  1038→  1038→				}
  1039→  1039→			}
  1040→  1040→			// Validate sessions array exists
  1041→  1041→			if sessions, ok := summary["sessions"].([]any); !ok || len(sessions) == 0 {
  1042→  1042→				env.T.Error("CheckpointSummary.sessions should have at least one entry")
  1043→  1043→			}
  1044→  1044→			// Validate files_touched if specified
  1045→  1045→			if len(v.FilesTouched) > 0 {
  1046→  1046→				if filesTouched, ok := summary["files_touched"].([]any); ok {
  1047→  1047→					touchedSet := make(map[string]bool)
  1048→  1048→					for _, f := range filesTouched {
  1049→  1049→						if s, ok := f.(string); ok {
  1050→  1050→							touchedSet[s] = true
  1051→  1051→						}
  1052→  1052→					}
  1053→  1053→					for _, expected := range v.FilesTouched {
  1054→  1054→						if !touchedSet[expected] {
  1055→  1055→							env.T.Errorf("CheckpointSummary.files_touched missing %q", expected)
  1056→  1056→						}
  1057→  1057→					}
  1058→  1058→				}
  1059→  1059→			}
  1060→  1060→		}

All tests pass. Let me summarize the fix:

**The Problem:**
When OpenCode makes commits mid-turn (before `turn-end`), the `post-commit` hook tries to read the transcript file for condensation. But the transcript file only gets created when `opencode export` is called, which previously only happened at `turn-end`. So the transcript was either missing or stale.

**The Fix:**
1. Added `PrepareTranscript` method to OpenCodeAgent implementing the `TranscriptPreparer` interface - this calls `opencode export` to refresh the transcript file

2. Modified `extractSessionDataFromLiveTranscript` in the condensation code to call `PrepareTranscript` before reading the transcript file

Now when the `post-commit` hook runs for mid-turn commits:
1. It calls `extractSessionDataFromLiveTranscript`
2. Which calls `PrepareTranscript` for OpenCode
3. Which calls `opencode export` to get the latest transcript with all the agent's actions
4. Then reads and processes the refreshed transcript

This ensures the transcript contains all agent actions up to the commit point, not just from the start of the turn.
